south-hero-vt.dogs: Split stop: the two Missisquoi NWR trails take a leashed dog under the refuge's own rule, but Vermont publishes nothing reachable for Mount Philo or Niquette Bay, so treat both state parks as unknown until Vermont State Parks is phoned.
south-hero-vt.dogs_source_quote: Pets must be leashed and under the control of the owner while on the refuge.

bismarck-nd.dogs: North Dakota's adopted park use rules allow pets on all Fort Abraham Lincoln trails on a leash of six feet or less, personally attended; only buildings, playgrounds, swimming areas and posted areas are closed to them — so the On-a-Slant earthlodges and the blockhouses mean leaving the dog outside.
bismarck-nd.dogs_source_quote: Pets shall be personally attended at all times and shall be effectively restrained by a portable enclosure or a leash not exceeding six feet [1.83 meters] in length.

trails: Mount Mansfield via Sunset Ridge / Long Trail
stowe-vt.authority: Vermont Dept. of Forests, Parks and Recreation / Vermont State Parks (C.C. Putnam State Forest, Mount Mansfield State Forest, Underhill State Park, Smugglers' Notch State Park), with the Green Mountain Club maintaining the Long Trail sections

https://vtstateparks.com/pets.html — 403

https://anr.vermont.gov/ — 403

https://www.greenmountainclub.org/hiking-with-dogs/ — loads, but publishes only general guidance, not a per-trail rule: 'Please observe all posted signage about dogs at the trailheads; note some areas such as the alpine zone will require your dog to be on a leash while other areas may not allow dogs'. It names Stowe Pinnacle in passing as a dog hike but states no permission.

Search index for vtstateparks.com and fpr.vermont.gov pet pages returned only third-party guides (dogtrailrules, petfriendlytravel, Burlington Free Press), never an official sentence

Aug 2026 pass — tried the rule as LAW rather than as a park page, since the park pages are the part that 403s. The adopted rule is Code of Vermont Rules 12 020 009, 'VISITOR CONDUCT AND FEES AND CHARGES FOR STATE PARK SERVICES AND COMMERCIAL ACTIVITIES ON DEPARTMENT LANDS'. Every route to its text failed, listed below.

https://secure.vermont.gov/SOS/rules/ — LOADS (so the Vermont 403 is not domain-wide, it is specific to the parks sites). But it carries PROPOSED rules only, and points to LexisNexis for adopted ones.

http://www.lexisnexis.com/hottopics/codeofvtrules/ — the Secretary of State's designated publisher of the Code of Vermont Rules. 301-redirects into advance.lexis.com, a JavaScript container that returns no rule text.
https://sos.vermont.gov/rules/ — 403
https://regulations.justia.com/states/vermont/agency-12/sub-agency-020/chapter-009/section-12-020-009/ — 403. This is the one page a search actually surfaced with the right citation, and it refused.

https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/vermont/12-020-009 — loads, but only as an agency index; Cornell LII carries no Vermont rule text at this citation (it does carry North Dakota's, which is how Bismarck was settled).

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=%22Vermont+State+Parks%22+rules+%22pets%22+leash+rabies+certificate+official+PDF — returned Burlington Free Press, Hipcamp and a vtstateparks.com tag page. No official rule text anywhere in the index.
stowe-vt.action: Phone Vermont State Parks on 1-888-409-7579 (or parks@vermont.gov) and ask two things: are dogs permitted on Mount Mansfield's Sunset Ridge and the Long Trail over the summit ridge, given the alpine zone, and is there any dog restriction on the Putnam State Forest trails at Stowe Pinnacle and Moss Glen Falls. One call settles all six. Worth doing before arrival — this is a 4-night hard-anchored stop on 1 Oct 2028 and the trails are most of what the stop is for.

homer.action: The Spit trail almost certainly takes a leashed dog, but the city does not say so and this project does not publish a rule it cannot source. Phone the Homer City Clerk on (907) 235-3130 (clerk@cityofhomer-ak.gov) and ask for the trail dog rule in Homer City Code Title 20 — one call covers the Spit trail and Diamond Creek, since both are city-managed. Ask Kachemak Heritage Land Trust separately for the Homestead Trail. NOTE: the reported 'voice control on the Homestead Trail' in the task brief came from a blog, not the land trust — it is not recorded here.

https://matsu.gov/trails — no pet or leash rule

https://matsu.gov/trails re-read for contacts — no pet rule, and it routes trail questions to the borough's Land & Resource Management Department.
talkeetna.action: Phone the Matanuska-Susitna Borough on (907) 861-7801 and ask for Land & Resource Management (which matsu.gov/trails names as the trails contact) or Parks, Recreation, Trails & Library Services. Ask one question: is there an ADOPTED borough ordinance requiring dogs to be leashed in borough parks, or are dogs simply permitted at Talkeetna Lakes Park with no published rule. Do not rely on the 2024 draft ordinance.

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=eurekaparks.com+Lake+Leatherwood+park+rules+regulations+dogs+leash+trails — same result: no official park-rules page indexed.

bentonville-ar.authority: Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, which owns and manages the 134-acre trail network including the Art Trail. The City of Bentonville does not manage this trail.
checked: https://crystalbridges.org/policies — the museum's own policies page. Covers photography, bags and drones ('drones are not permitted on the museum's trails and grounds') but says nothing about pets, dogs or service animals.
https://crystalbridges.org/visit/nature-trails — the official trails page, which names the Art Trail and seven other trails. No pet, dog or leash rule.
https://crystalbridges.org/visit/ — the main visit page. No mention of dogs, pets, animals or service animals.

https://lite.duckduckgo.com/lite/?q=Crystal+Bridges+Museum+trails+dogs+leashed+pets+policy+crystalbridges.org — the 'leashed pets are welcome on the museum trails' claim traces only to BringFido and similar aggregators, not to the museum.

Aug 2026 pass — no new sources attempted. The three museum pages above are the museum's complete published policy surface and a private landowner has no code, statute or administrative rule to fall back on, which is the route that settled Bismarck. This one only a phone call can close.
bentonville-ar.action: Phone Crystal Bridges Guest Services on 479-657-2335 and ask whether leashed dogs are allowed on the Art Trail and the wider museum trail network, and whether the rule differs on the paved North Forest / Orchard sections. One call settles the whole stop, since the Art Trail is the only trail on the card.
